about: Local-knowledge workaround tips. A tip is attached to a disruption when ALL of its filters match (lines, causes, modes, stations, effects). Keep them short, factual and checkable. Shown in the app as 'Local tip'.

tips.text: S-Bahn trunk line (Pasing – Hauptbahnhof – Marienplatz – Ostbahnhof) in trouble? The U5 runs almost parallel: Laimer Platz – Hauptbahnhof – Karlsplatz – Odeonsplatz – Ostbahnhof. Tram 19 also links Pasing, Hauptbahnhof, Karlsplatz and Max-Weber-Platz.
U3/U6 trouble in the centre? Trams 27 and 28 link Schwabing (Kurfürstenplatz) with Karlsplatz and Sendlinger Tor, and the U2 connects Scheidplatz with Hauptbahnhof and Sendlinger Tor.
Short U1/U2 interruption? Hauptbahnhof ↔ Sendlinger Tor is about a 12-minute walk along Sonnenstraße, which is often quicker than waiting.
U4/U5 trouble? Between Hauptbahnhof and Ostbahnhof any S-Bahn on the trunk line is the fastest alternative; tram 19 runs Hauptbahnhof – Karlsplatz – Max-Weber-Platz.
Tram replacement buses usually stop on the street next to the tram stop and carry fewer people. If you're near a U-Bahn station, switching is often faster.
Match days: after full time, walking about 15 minutes south to Kieferngarten (U6) often beats the queues at Fröttmaning.
Avoid changing trains at Marienplatz at peak market times: Odeonsplatz (U3/U6, U4/U5) and Karlsplatz (S-Bahn, U4/U5) are less crowded.
MVG strikes don't stop the S-Bahn (Deutsche Bahn), regional trains or most MVV regional buses. In the centre, walking or bike-sharing is often quicker than waiting.
Marches usually hold up buses and trams on surface streets for 30–60 minutes; the U-Bahn underneath keeps running.
Lift out of order? Check MVG's lift status before setting off and plan to use the next station with a working lift. Staff at major hubs can help.
Buses stuck in traffic? A nearby U-Bahn or S-Bahn line is usually faster until the road clears.
